topic_name: Uses of Primary and Modal Auxiliary Verbs

questions.question: You ______ not enter without permission.
______ I come in, Sir?
questions.explanation: 'May' is the formal modal auxiliary for seeking permission.

questions.question: She ______ speak five languages fluently.
questions.explanation: 'Can' denotes general ability in the present.

questions.question: We ______ respect our national flag.
questions.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses moral obligation or duty.

questions.question: You ______ see a doctor immediately; you look very sick.
He ______ have missed the train; that's why he is late.
questions.explanation: 'Must have + V3' expresses a strong logical deduction about a past event.

questions.question: You ______ not smoke in public places.
questions.explanation: 'Must not' expresses legal or strict prohibition.

questions.question: ______ you please lend me your pen?
questions.explanation: 'Could you please...' expresses a polite request.

questions.question: Would you mind ______ the window?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'Would you mind' is followed by a gerund (-ing form).

questions.question: I ______ rather starve than beg.
You had better ______ at once.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' is followed by a bare infinitive (V1 without 'to').

questions.question: He ______ play cricket when he was young.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' expresses a discontinued past habit.

questions.question: She is used to ______ up early in the morning.
questions.explanation: 'Be used to' (accustomed to) takes a gerund (-ing form).

questions.question: How ______ you speak to me like that?
questions.explanation: 'How dare you...' expresses indignation or anger.

questions.question: You ______ not come tomorrow; it is a holiday.
questions.explanation: 'Need not' expresses absence of obligation or necessity.

questions.question: Walk carefully lest you ______ stumble.
questions.explanation: The conjunction 'lest' is always followed by the modal auxiliary 'should'.

questions.question: ______ God bless you with good health!
questions.explanation: 'May' expresses wishes, prayers, and blessings in optative sentences.

questions.question: It ______ rain this evening; look at the dark clouds.
questions.explanation: 'May' expresses strong possibility based on present evidence.

questions.question: Take an umbrella; it ______ rain later.
questions.explanation: 'Might' expresses a remote or weak possibility.

questions.question: I ______ like to invite the chief guest to speak.
questions.explanation: 'Would like to' is a polite expression for expressing desire or intent.

questions.question: ______ we start the meeting now?
questions.explanation: 'Shall we...?' is used with 1st person plural for suggestions or offers.

questions.question: You ______ have informed me earlier; now it is too late.
questions.explanation: 'Should have + V3' expresses past obligation or regret about an unfulfilled action.

questions.question: He ______ swim across the river when he was twenty.
questions.explanation: 'Could' expresses general ability in the past.

questions.question: She ______ not do such a thing; she is too kind.
questions.explanation: 'Could not' expresses past impossibility or disbelief.

questions.question: Candidates ______ answer any five questions.
You ______ not worry about the finances; I will manage.
______ you have another cup of tea?
questions.explanation: 'Will you have...?' is used for polite offers and invitations.

questions.question: We ______ obey the traffic regulations.
questions.explanation: 'Must' indicates legal necessity and compulsory compliance.

questions.question: ______ I carry your bag for you?
questions.explanation: 'Shall I...?' is used to make a polite offer of assistance.

questions.question: He said he ______ come the next day.
questions.explanation: 'Would' is the past form of 'will' in reported speech.

questions.question: If I had money, I ______ buy that car.
We ______ to love our neighbours.
questions.explanation: 'Ought' is followed by 'to' to express moral duty.

questions.question: You ______ not have spoken so rudely to him.
questions.explanation: 'Should not have + V3' criticizes past undesirable action.

questions.question: He ______ be over sixty; he looks so young.
questions.explanation: 'Cannot be' expresses strong logical impossibility in the present.

questions.question: She ______ be at home; the lights are on.
questions.explanation: 'Must be' expresses strong logical deduction in the present.

questions.question: They ______ have reached Delhi by now.
questions.explanation: 'Must have' indicates probable certainty about the past.

questions.question: You ______ leave now if you have finished your work.
Children ______ obey their parents.
We ______ rather walk than take a taxi.
I had better ______ my coat; it's freezing.
He ______ not dare to oppose his boss.
questions.explanation: When used as an ordinary verb, 'dare' takes auxiliary 'does not dare'.

questions.question: You ______ not have bought so much food; half of it was wasted.
questions.explanation: 'Need not have + V3' means an action was performed but was unnecessary.

questions.question: She ______ sing like an angel.
If it rains, we ______ cancel the trip.
He ______ rather die than betray his country.
Work hard lest you ______ fail.
______ peace be upon you!
You ______ not drive without a valid driving license.
I ______ rather drink tea than coffee.
He ______ be the new manager; he is wearing the badge.
questions.explanation: Logical deduction based on visual proof -> 'must be'.

questions.question: The principal ______ to address the students tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'is to address' indicates a planned official arrangement.

questions.question: I ______ have helped him if I had known his trouble.
You ______ pay your taxes on time.
______ I open the door for you?
questions.explanation: 'Shall I...?' is an offer of help.

questions.question: You ______ have locked the car; someone could steal it.
questions.explanation: 'Ought to have + V3' indicates past moral/sensible duty.

questions.question: She ______ not touch that snake; she was terrified.
questions.explanation: 'Dared not' expresses lack of courage in past.

questions.question: He ______ to work late hours during tax season.
We ______ protect our environment.
You ______ not have shouted at the child.
questions.explanation: 'Should not have' expresses regret/criticism of past action.

questions.question: The train ______ arrive at 10 AM as per the schedule.
questions.explanation: 'Should' expresses expected probability based on schedule.

questions.question: ______ you have some more dessert?
questions.explanation: 'Would you have...?' is a polite invitation.

questions.question: He ______ not enter the room without knocking.
I ______ rather stay at home tonight.
You had better ______ a doctor before it worsens.
She ______ have forgotten about the appointment.
questions.explanation: 'Might have' expresses a possible past explanation.

questions.question: ______ I borrow your camera for the weekend?
questions.explanation: 'Could I borrow...?' is a polite informal/formal request.

questions.question: Every citizen ______ abide by the Constitution.
You ______ not have spent all your savings.
questions.explanation: 'Should not have spent' expresses criticism of unwise past action.

questions.question: He ______ be asleep; he worked night shift.
We ______ to respect all religions.
He said that he ______ solve the riddle.
______ that I were a billionaire!
questions.explanation: 'Would that...' is an archaic/literary idiom expressing strong wish.

questions.question: Run fast lest you ______ miss the train.
You ______ not bring your own food into the cinema hall.
I ______ speak Tamil, but I cannot write it.
She ______ rather resign than accept a bribe.
You had better ______ an umbrella; the sky is overcast.
Nobody ______ dare to question his authority.
We ______ to be kind to animals.
You ______ not worry; everything will be fine.
______ long live the King!
He ______ have reached by now if the flight was on time.
You ______ not copy answers in the exam hall.
I ______ rather fail with honor than cheat.
He had better ______ the truth to the police.
They ______ to have arrived two hours ago.
questions.explanation: 'Ought to have arrived' denotes unfulfilled expectation.

questions.question: She ______ play the violin beautifully.
______ you mind turning down the volume?
questions.explanation: 'Would you mind...' is a polite request idiom.

questions.question: You ______ not have bought that expensive watch.
It ______ be true; I can't believe it!
He ______ be at his desk; his computer is logged in.
You ______ carry your ID card during the exam.
We ______ to help the injured victims.
He ______ swim five miles when he was in the navy.
______ you have some fresh orange juice?
I ______ rather sleep on the floor than in that dirty bed.
He had better ______ his doctor's advice.
______ God give you courage to face this tragedy!
You ______ not pay for this; it is completely free.
questions.explanation: 'Need not pay' expresses absence of necessity.

questions.question: Drive slowly lest an accident ______ happen.
She ______ have reached the summit by this time.
He ______ not enter the dark forest alone.
You ______ not park your vehicle in front of the gate.
I ______ rather learn Malayalam than any other language.
You ______ respect your elders and teachers.
______ you have a safe flight!
Candidates ______ write on both sides of the paper.
You ______ not smoke inside the petrol pump.
We ______ help those who are in distress.
He ______ speak four languages fluently.
When I was young, I ______ run ten miles without stopping.
______ I use your mobile phone for an urgent call?
questions.explanation: 'May I...' is formal request for permission.

questions.question: You ______ leave the hall after submitting the answer sheet.
She ______ have reached home by now.
He ______ be at the library; he always studies there on Saturdays.
Take an umbrella; it ______ rain later in the afternoon.
The clouds are very dark; it ______ rain heavily soon.
questions.explanation: 'May' expresses strong possibility based on visible evidence.

questions.question: You had better ______ the truth to the police.
He would rather ______ than tell a lie.
Work hard lest you ______ fail the exam.
Walk carefully lest you ______ slip.
You ______ not have spoken to your mother so rudely.
questions.explanation: 'Should not have + V3' expresses criticism of past action.

questions.question: They ______ to have informed us about the delay.
How ______ you enter my room without knocking?
You ______ not buy tickets; entry is completely free.
We ______ obey the traffic rules.
______ you please pass the water jug?
questions.explanation: 'Could you please...' is a polite request.

questions.question: Would you mind ______ the window?
He ______ play football every evening when he was at school.
She is used to ______ in noisy environments.
He said that he ______ attend the meeting the next day.
questions.explanation: 'Would' is the past modal of 'will' in reported speech.

questions.question: If I had wings, I ______ fly across the oceans.
If he had invited me, I ______ attended the party.
He ______ not dare to challenge his father's decision.
questions.explanation: Ordinary verb 'dare' takes auxiliary 'does not dare'.

questions.question: You ______ have watered the plants; it rained all day.
questions.explanation: 'Need not have + V3' indicates an unnecessary past action.

questions.question: He ______ be over seventy; he walks with great difficulty.
That news ______ be true; I spoke to him just five minutes ago.
______ I carry this heavy suitcase for you?
questions.explanation: 'Shall I...?' is an offer of help.

questions.question: ______ we begin our session now?
You ______ not park your vehicle in front of the gate.
We ______ rather die on our feet than live on our knees.
You had better ______ the medicines on time.
Every citizen ______ respect the national anthem.
She ______ sing melodiously.
______ that I were a bird!
He ______ have forgotten his wallet at home.
Children ______ obey their elders.
______ peace prevail across the world!
I ______ rather sleep on the floor than in that damp bed.
He had better ______ his coat; the wind is icy.
They ______ to have completed the assignment yesterday.
She ______ play the piano when she was just six.
You ______ not have wasted all that food.
It ______ be a mistake; let me check again.
You ______ always stand by the truth.
